title: Overview: the big ideas
summary: The chapter's key concepts and how its sections fit together.

blocks.md: Welcome to **Operating Agents** (Vol III). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

An offline evaluation picks its tasks, fixtures, and graders in advance, and live traffic honors none of those choices. Production brings inputs no fixture anticipated, dependencies that slow down under load, and tool results cut short without warning, while every admitted task acts with real authority. When the rate of accepted tasks drops, the count says that something failed but not where, because one trial spreads its model calls, tool executions, and checks across processes and hosts.

nodes.label: From Offline Verdict to Live Operation

rows: Spans bind every model call, mediated tool execution, and check to their trial and artifact, but a diagnostic trace may sample or drop and never replaces the durable recovery log or the verdict record.
Sampling may thin diagnostic detail but never the accounting record of admitted trials, verdicts, spend, and drops, and retention is chosen per verdict under storage and privacy budgets.
An agent incident is diagnosed by keeping findings separated by boundary and testing each with a controlled intervention on the recorded trajectory, not by naming one culprit.
Release exposure is staged so each stage answers its own question (offline gate, shadow execution, bounded canary), with sequential monitoring and hard tripwires that stop admission.
A release decision is a declared conjunctive rule written before data and applied to an evidence record that keeps verdicts, paired cohorts, and diagnostics.
The longest chain of dependent operations recorded in the trace is measured from span timing, and only work on it can shorten the trajectory.
Release is justified by a scoped, inspectable safety case of claim, argument, evidence, assumptions, and residual uncertainty, and evidence for one claim does not establish the others.
